content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to PLCs and home automation. I'm wondering if [company_name] [product_name] can work with soft touch switches (such as those from Livolo). Alternatively, are there any other brands compatible with the [product_name] soft touch switch for 120/220 Volt, 60 Hz? Thank you.

The phrase "soft touch switch (Livolo switch)" may be familiar to you, but not necessarily to others in this forum, including myself. Could you share a [document] or a [url] with product details or specifications?

A Livolo switch will not work directly with a [product_name] device. Livolo switches require at least 1 Watt of output power. If you install a resistor between the input of the [product_name] and the neutral line, it should work. The appropriate resistor depends on your power supply (about 50 kOhm for 230 Volt) – keep in mind, the resistor consumes 1 Watt and might become hot. You need to use the 230V version of the [product_name], which operates on 115–240 VAC.
Hello, The switch uses capacitive touch control – I should have clarified that earlier. I don't want switches that are controlled by RF, like LIVOLO RF models.
I could use the 230 Volt version of the [product_name], but I will need a transformer for it. Does [company_name] offer capacitive touch switches?

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are investigating how [company_name] [product_name] interacts with capacitive (soft touch) wall switches, specifically from Livolo, for home automation. There are difficulties as Livolo switches need a minimum power threshold that [product_name] inputs do not supply by default. Users are seeking clarification on the technical limitations and prefer an integrated [company_name] solution for capacitive switching.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [company_name] [product_name] to support or directly connect with capacitive soft touch wall switches, and are interested in [company_name] alternatives for such touch control. They are seeking an out-of-the-box solution without needing complex add-ons.
